description:
Refusals and the builtins at their edge: `exec`, `source`, `bind`, `history`, `enable`, `ulimit`
and `fc`.

Each case name starts with `refusals: `.

cases.name: refusals: exec ls -l is not exec -l
refusals: exec wc -l is not exec -l
refusals: exec sort -c is not exec -c
refusals: exec -- passes through to the command

stderr.text: bash: exec -a, -c and -l are unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture (exec -a/-l): -a and -l are documented refusals; the oracle's coreutils multiplexer, not bash, produces the comparison output for a real run

cases.name: refusals: exec -a name is still refused

cases.name: refusals: a failed exec ends the script
refusals: a successful exec still ends the script
refusals: a failed exec ends the subshell it's in
refusals: a successful exec ends the subshell it's in
cases.script: (exec echo hi; echo notreached); echo after

cases.name: refusals: read -e reads plainly from input that is no terminal
refusals: mapfile -C runs its callback
cases.script: printf 'a\nb\n' | mapfile -C echo -c 1 arr; echo done=$?

expected.reason: fixture: a canonical refusal for a Brush placeholder Bash itself implements; not a WASI limit, but implementing readline/dlopen/job-control/man-pages is out of scope

stderr.text: bash: source of /dev/stdin, /dev/stdout or /dev/stderr is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: sourcing a live stream would block forever in this single-threaded cooperative model before the pipeline feeding it could run; a documented refusal, not a WASI limit

cases.name: refusals: source searches PATH
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/fixes-sourcepath; echo 'echo hi from sourced' >/tmp/fixes-sourcepath/myfile.sh; PATH="/tmp/fixes-sourcepath:$PATH" source myfile.sh

cases.name: refusals: sourced syntax error names the file
cases.script: printf 'echo ok\nif then\n' >/tmp/fixes-badsrc.sh; source /tmp/fixes-badsrc.sh; echo after=$?

stderr.text:
/tmp/fixes-badsrc.sh: line 2: syntax error near unexpected token `then'
/tmp/fixes-badsrc.sh: line 2: `if then'

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool's documented all-or-nothing preflight (README.md) means nothing before a later syntax error runs either, unlike bash itself, which executes each command as it is read

cases.name: refusals: sourced runtime error names the file
refusals: bind binding form warns and succeeds

stderr.text: bash: bind's query options (-l, -p, -P, -s, -S, -v, -V, -q, -u, -X) are unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: bash's own readline tables are compiled in and answer these queries even under `bash -c` (confirmed against the oracle: `bind -q abort` succeeds, printing bash's own warning and then its real answer) -- Brush has no equivalent table built, not a WASI/terminal limit; reproducing bash's actual emacs/vi defaults just for these query forms is disproportionate

cases.name: refusals: history -c clears
cases.script: history -s foo; history -c; history; echo s=$?

cases.name: refusals: history -d deletes an offset
cases.script: history -s foo; history -s bar; history -d 1; history

cases.name: refusals: history -w then -r round-trips a file
cases.script: history -s foo; history -w /tmp/fixes-histfile-wr; history -c; history -r /tmp/fixes-histfile-wr; history

refusals: history rejects a non-numeric N

stderr.text: bash: ulimit is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: a documented refusal (README.md's "Commands" section) this platform genuinely cannot support -- WASI has no resource limits (ulimit), no history list to edit (fc), and no argv[0] override (exec -a)
